Don't worry, natural beta carotene will not hurt you. Worst case scenario is when people turn orange from eating only carrots. Synthetic beta carotene can hurt you, especially if you're a smoker, but natural forms found in fruits and vegetables will not hurt you because your body will only convert as much vitamin A from beta carotene as you need. "β-Carotene, a precursor form of vitamin A typical of vegetable sources such as carrots, is selectively converted into retinoids, so it does not cause hypervitaminosis A; however, overconsumption can cause carotenosis, a benign condition in which the skin turns orange.

The proportion of carotenoids absorbed decreases as dietary intake increases. Within the intestinal wall (mucosa), β-carotene is partially converted into vitamin A (retinol) by an enzyme, dioxygenase. This mechanism is regulated by the individual's vitamin A status. If the body has enough vitamin A, the conversion of β-carotene decreases. Therefore, β-carotene is a very safe source of vitamin A and high intakes will not lead to hypervitaminosis A. Excess β-carotene is predominantly stored in the fat tissues of the body. The adult's fat stores are often yellow from accumulated carotene while the infant's fat stores are white. Excessive intake of β-carotene leads to yellowish skin, but this is quickly reversible upon cessation of intake.[23]" - Wikipedia on beta carotene.

First of all, I think our insistence that a machine can be made intelligent is absurd. We still don't have a consensus on what 'intelligence' is. So we certainly can't jump straight to it.

Second, the idea that a machine can understand and articulate non-absolutes - like morals and ethics - when we again don't have consensus, is absurd.
